title: rest, runtime: a body `expectedVersion` of `''` or `false` hides `If-Match` on `PATCH /data/:object/:id`, so an update sent with a stale `If-Match` is applied unguarded, on both doors
body:
Filing gate **①**, class **(a)**: a concurrency guard the caller sent is silently dropped, so a stale write is applied. It was measured at a public door. This is #13576's class (an empty token silently opting out of the check), on the body spelling.

`reach:` HTTP, measured once by #23462's dev (`os-dev-report` `6169083704`, out-of-scope finding 2).
- **The setup:** a real `@objectstack/hono` `createHonoApp`, and separately a rig over `RestServer`'s registered `PATCH` handler.
- **The request:** a body `{ name, expectedVersion: '' }` with a **stale** `If-Match`.
- **The result:** `200`, and the row was written, on both. A body `expectedVersion: false` behaves the same way.

Filed by `domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01Q9PZ5Pzqcus4woVvTZwWNU`, at PR #23490's ACCEPT. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane and grade are triage's.

**Reader who acts:** triage grades it. Both landings are `domain:cli` by the lane table:
- `RestServer`'s `PATCH` in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (about `:9021`-`:9024`, read on `main` `0d3ea295d1`);
- the dispatcher's `PATCH` branch in `packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts`, which PR #23490 makes REST's mirror, on purpose, so the two doors stay alike.

## What happens

Both doors compute `bodyVersion ?? If-Match` and then forward a token only when it is truthy.
- `''` and `false` are not nullish, so `If-Match` is never read.
- They are falsy, so no token is forwarded.
- So the update runs unguarded beside the stale `If-Match` the caller sent.

The protocol refuses a quoted-empty `""` (#13576), but it never sees this request, because the door drops the token first.

## Governing text

The ADR-0008 precondition family: `If-Match` and `expectedVersion` on a write are honoured or refused, never ignored. #13576 (closed) is the same rule for the header spelling.

`Seam: spec:UpdateDataRequest.expectedVersion → rest: rest-server.ts PATCH + runtime: domains/data.ts PATCH branch (consumer: every /data update that sends a version)`.

## Acceptance (a proposal; triage's call)

- A request that carries a version token in any spelling is either judged or refused. It is never applied unguarded. For example, a present but empty or non-string-or-number body `expectedVersion` is refused `400`, as the protocol refuses `""`. Or it falls through to `If-Match`. Pick one rule; ⛔ not two.
- One fix lands in both doors together, keeping them alike, as PR #23490 does.
- Pins on both doors: `''` and `false` each beside a stale `If-Match`, and beside no header.
- **Order:** after PR #23490 lands. It edits the same `data.ts` branch.

## Noted beside it, not filed

These are from the same report, in PR #23490's Acceptance notes, carrier none:
- `?expectedVersion` as a query on `PATCH` is read by neither door. The spec declares the `PATCH` token only as the body field or `If-Match`.
- The declared-endpoint door (`endpoint-executor.ts`, `object_operation` update) reads no token. That is a read-only inference, unmeasured.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `expectedVersion empty string or false in PATCH body skips If-Match, stale update applied`. It returned 4 hits: #23462 and #23265 (the dispatcher's dropped tokens, not this), and #22114 and #14393 (closed, not this). #13576 is the header twin, closed.

Dedupe words: expectedVersion empty string If-Match ignored; falsy body token skips If-Match stale update applied; PATCH data expectedVersion false.
